name: NVIDIA B300 (Blackwell Ultra)
memory_bandwidth_basis: 279GB HBM3E | 8 TB/s as printed for the GB300 NVL72 column; the HGX B300 column is 270GB | 7.7 TB/s. Dual reticle-limited dies presented as one GPU, as with B200.
notes: CONTESTED / transcription-damaged source. The Blackwell Ultra datasheet prints per-GPU: FP4 '20 PFLOPS | 15 PFLOPS', FP8/FP6 '10 PFLOPS | 9 PFLOPS', INT8 '330 TOPS | 307 TOPS', FP16/BF16 '5 PFLOPS | 4.5 PFLOPS', TF32 '2.5 PFLOPS | 2.2 PFLOPS', FP32 '80 TFLOPS | 75 TFLOPS', FP64 '1.3 TFLOPS | 1.2 TFLOPS'. Two columns, one presumably GB300 NVL72 and one HGX B300. Same 'dense is one-half of sparse' rule as Blackwell, so dense FP4 = 10 and 7.5 PFLOPS. FLAGGED: (1) the INT8 row reads 330/307 TOPS, which is ~30x too low - INT8 should track FP8 at ~10,000 TOPS sparse; this looks like a broken text-layer extraction (possibly '10 POPS'). INT8 IS THEREFORE NOT RECORDED in flops. (2) The two rows above both list precision fp8 (the sheet has separate FP8 and FP8/FP6 rows); they are kept separate to preserve the two printed columns. (3) B300's headline gain over B200 is memory (288GB vs 186GB, +1.5x) and attention-layer acceleration (2x) and PCIe Gen6 (256 GB/s), NOT raw Tensor FLOPS - FP4/FP8/FP16/TF32 are identical to B200 per GPU. tdp_w 1400 is the GB300 NVL72 'configurable up to 1,400W' figure (HGX B300 is 1,100W). vram_gb 288 chosen from the GB300 column; the HGX B300 column is 270GB. Reseller-hosted copy of NVIDIA's PDF. The 'other' row is FP64/FP64 Tensor Core (1.3 TFLOPS printed) - this schema's precision enum has no fp64 member. Also note this is a REMARKABLE REGRESSION from B200's 40 TFLOPS: Blackwell Ultra cuts FP64 by ~30x to satisfy export-control thresholds, which is why it cannot be slotted into HPC double-precision work.
